A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new theory of the semantics of natural language that is based on the idea that linguistic meanings are instructions for how to construct concepts, that is, for how to build mental representations of the world.

we are developing a theory of linguistic meaning which has a strong internalist orientation. But we also believe that the theory can accommodate some of the most powerful considerations which motivate externalist theories of meaning.

the meaning of a word is a concept that can be accessed by using the word, and the meaning of a sentence is the concept that is built up by combining the concepts accessed by using the words in the sentence.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can make sense of the idea that the meaning of a linguistic expression is an instruction for how to build a mental representation of a special kind, and that the meanings of different expressions can be combined to build more complex meanings.
